rules.source: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares — https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/123648/Ley_Federal_de_Protecci_n_de_Datos_Personales_en_Posesi_n_de_los.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Objective: protect personal data in the possession of private entities, regulating its legitimate, controlled and informed treatment to guarantee privacy and informational self-determination.

rules.source: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares + Ley General de los Derechos de Niñas, Niños y Adolescentes — https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LFPDPPP.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: In the treatment of personal data of minors, consent from a parent or guardian must always be obtained, prioritizing the best interests of the child ('interés superior de la niñez').

rules.source: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares — https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/123648/Ley_Federal_de_Protecci_n_de_Datos_Personales_en_Posesi_n_de_los.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Guardian/parental consent required for processing minors' personal data; best-interest-of-the-child principle applies, informed by Mexico's ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

rules.source: Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor (PROFECO) — https://www.profeco.gob.mx/juridico/pdf/l_lfpc_ultimo_camdip.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Object of the law: promote and protect consumer rights, ensure equity, certainty and legal security between providers and consumers, including protection of life/health/safety and adequate/clear product information. Enforced by PROFECO, published in Diario Oficial de la Federación 1992-12-24.

rules.source: No enacted comprehensive AI statute as of September 2026 — Mexico has adopted a hybrid, sectoral approach rather than a single AI law. A comprehensive National Law to Regulate the Use of Artificial Intelligence (introduced by Senator Karina Ruíz Ruíz) and a separate Federal Law Initiative for Ethical, Sovereign and Inclusive AI Development remain in the legislative process, not yet passed. The one enacted, narrower reform: amendments to the Federal Labor Law and Copyright Law protecting performers'/creators' voice and image against generative AI, published 14 May 2026. — https://cms.law/en/int/expert-guides/ai-regulation-scanner/mexico
rules.retrieved_snippet: Mexico reached the second half of 2026 without a general AI law; a comprehensive bill remains in Senate committee. The only enacted AI-related change so far is the May 2026 Labor/Copyright Law amendment on generative-AI voice/image protection.

rules.source: Ley General para la Inclusión de las Personas con Discapacidad + Ley Federal de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (2014) — https://www.gob.mx/conadis
rules.retrieved_snippet: Mexico's primary disability-rights statute protects and promotes inclusion broadly; the Federal Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law separately mandates that telecommunications services be accessible to persons with disabilities. Neither law explicitly names website/digital-content accessibility standards (e.g. no codified WCAG requirement) — website accessibility specifically is honestly underdeveloped in Mexican federal law as of this research, not a settled, citable requirement the way it is in the EU, Poland, or Brazil's LBI.

rules.source: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (new law, DOF 20-03-2025, replacing the 2010 law) — https://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Documentos/Federal/html/wo125102.html
rules.retrieved_snippet: Article 1: 'La presente Ley es de orden público y de observancia general en todo el territorio nacional'; regulates handling of personal data held by private parties. Article 2 fr. XV names the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno as the competent authority. The Cámara de Diputados consolidated text is reported (search result) to reflect a reform of 14-11-2025; the diputados.gob.mx site was unreachable so this was not read directly.

rules.source: Código Penal Federal, Título Noveno, Art. 211 bis 1 (state-government mirror compiled through DOF 08-02-2006) — http://siga.jalisco.gob.mx/assets/documentos/normatividad/CodPenalFed.htm
rules.retrieved_snippet: Art. 211 bis 1 begins 'Al que sin autorización modifique, destruya o provoque pérdida de información contenida en sistemas o equipos de informática...'; in the retrieved (older) text the penalty is six months to two years of prison and a fine of 100 to 300 days. Reform proposals and a 2019 chamber vote to raise penalties exist; current federal text/penalties NOT verified.

rules.source: Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor (DOF 24-12-1996; page shows reform of 01-07-2020) — http://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Documentos/Federal/html/wo17068.html
rules.retrieved_snippet: Article 1: the law 'tiene por objeto la salvaguarda y promoción del acervo cultural de la Nación' and the protection of the rights of authors, performers, publishers, producers and broadcasters over their works.

rules.source: Ley para Regular las Instituciones de Tecnología Financiera (Ley Fintech) — https://www.cnbv.gob.mx/Normatividad/Ley%20para%20Regular%20las%20Instituciones%20de%20Tecnolog%C3%ADa%20Financiera.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Article 1 (as returned by search of the CNBV text): the law is of public order and general observance and 'tiene por objeto regular los servicios financieros que prestan las instituciones de tecnología financiera'.

rules.source: Ley Fintech (CNBV text) and Banco de México Circular 4/2019 — https://www.cnbv.gob.mx/Normatividad/Ley%20para%20Regular%20las%20Instituciones%20de%20Tecnolog%C3%ADa%20Financiera.pdf ; https://www.banxico.org.mx/marco-normativo/normativa-emitida-por-el-banco-de-mexico/circular-4-2019/%7B8D7769AF-03F6-701A-68AA-EF25A73AD035%7D.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Per search results of the official texts: ITFs may operate only with the virtual assets determined by Banco de México in general provisions and need Banxico's prior authorization; Circular 4/2019 determines which virtual assets and conditions. Circular dates from 2019 (régimen currency in 2026 not verified).
